what: Official implementation of RRSI — regularized recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses. A single search core drives three Domain instances (coding, workspace, engineering-design), drafting, screening and evaluating harness candidates in git worktrees and fast-forwarding the branch to each winner.
architecture: One core, three instances: rrsi/ holds the search loop (evaluate, propose, analyst, digester, critic, selection, history, schedule, components); each domains/<name>/ is a Domain adapter (evolve/heldout/smoke splits, run/score, leakage denylist, guards) plus its starting harness and rrsi.json hyperparameters.

Candidates in git worktrees: every candidate harness is drafted, screened and evaluated in its own worktree on a branch off evolve/<domain>; accepting one fast-forwards the branch, so the incumbent is always a commit and the edit history (one JSONL record per edit: component, hypothesis, score/cost change, verdict) is auditable.

Method-to-code is explicit: the annealed budget in schedule.py, history/stall/exploration in history.py, the critic leakage screen in critic.py, the noise-adjusted floor + cost rule in selection.py, and novelty over structural component types in components.py.
advantages: The regularization discipline ships as runnable pure functions with named per-instance constants, not prose. selection.py states Algorithm 2 verbatim — admissible iff S' >= S* - delta and either the token-budget rule [Delta C <= beta0 + beta1 Delta S] when Delta S > delta or the band rule [w_s Delta S - w_c Delta C + w_n nu(l') > 0] otherwise, then H_{t+1} = argmax admissible S' — while schedule.py computes b_t = ceil(b_min + (b_max - b_min) * (1 + cos(pi t / T)) / 2) and domains/coding/rrsi.json pins delta = 0.017, beta0 = 0.10, beta1 = 44.5, w_s = 0.0, w_c = 15.0, w_n = 0.5. An rsif-style val gate can therefore be borrowed as a calibrated function rather than re-derived from a paper.

The Domain adapter is a hard, documented boundary, and the evidence spans substrates rather than one benchmark. Adding a domain is one domains/<name>/adapter.py exporting DOMAIN with evolve_ids/heldout_ids/smoke_ids, run/score, load_trial/render_trace/task_row, smoke, and critic_patterns/component_signals/briefs/guards; the core never reads a trajectory format or a benchmark directory itself. The same loop is then instantiated on container work (Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89 tasks x k=2 = 178 trials), document work (Harvey LAB) and engineering design (EngDesign, with non-compensatory guards a scalar score cannot express: valid-rate drop, no-submission rise), under both Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.5 Flash as the frozen policy.

The worktree-plus-JSONL design makes the search auditable, resumable and replayable instead of a black box. The incumbent is always a commit on evolve/<domain>; every edit carries a component tag validated against the fixed vocabulary K of 9 tags, with a diff-derived recovery path in components.py (text_only -> prompt, then domain signals, then generic ToolRegistry/skills//Memory( patterns) so a mislabelled prompt tweak cannot pass as a skill; and readjudicate --t <t> re-applies Algorithm 2 to a stored round while reevaluate --t <t> re-measures one after an infrastructure failure.
run: Python 3.10+, plus per-instance environments (harbor for the coding instance; a Python 3.11 env with `pip install -e .[agentic]` for workspace/engineering). Point the roles at a LiteLLM model string (default Claude Opus 4.8 on Vertex AI: set VERTEX_PROJECT / VERTEXAI_PROJECT and VERTEX_LOCATION / VERTEXAI_LOCATION; RRSI_VERTEX_PROJECTS takes a comma-separated list and spreads the search roles' calls round-robin). Then `python3 rrsi.py --domain coding smoke` (liveness: compile, construct, a couple of tasks), `baseline`, `run`, `status`; `--T/--k/--delta/--beta1` override rrsi.json, and `readjudicate --t <t>` re-applies Algorithm 2 to a stored round while `reevaluate --t <t>` re-measures one after an infrastructure failure.
note: Read domains/<name>/rrsi.json and the method-to-code table in the README to see each regularization rule as an actual function — especially selection.py (noise-adjusted floor + cost rule) and critic.py (leakage screen), which are the concrete, copyable forms of the discipline rsif encodes as its val gate and held-out gates.
_source_note: Verified against the repo, not just the README: readme via `gh api repos/google-research/rrsi/readme`, the full recursive file tree, and source for rrsi/selection.py (Algorithm 2 docstring: Delta S / Delta C, token-budget vs w_s/w_c/w_n band, floor S' >= S* - delta, argmax), rrsi/schedule.py (cosine-annealed b_t, bounds ||z_t||_0 only), rrsi/components.py (K = prompt/control_flow/config/output_plumbing/context_mgmt/client_tool/skill/memory/subagent; K_str = client_tool/skill/memory/subagent; classify_diff recovery), rrsi/critic.py (deterministic generic+domain denylist then LLM review, bounded repair rounds, an unrepairable candidate recorded without measurement), domains/coding/rrsi.json (T=20, k=2, m=2, b_min/b_max = 1/4, delta=0.017, w_s=0.0, w_c=15.0, w_n=0.5, beta1=44.5, policy_model vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-8, terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1, swe-bench/swe-bench-verified), domains/coding/README.md (89 tasks, k=2, Terminus-2 H_0) and pyproject.toml (requires-python >=3.10; dev/agentic/coding extras). Architecture, what and note reproduce the existing card verbatim — every claim in them checked out. One field corrected: `run` named only VERTEX_PROJECT/VERTEX_LOCATION and omitted the liveness step; the README and domains/coding/README also require the VERTEXAI_* aliases and RRSI_VERTEX_PROJECTS (roles spread calls round-robin), and list `smoke` before `baseline`. High confidence.
